clean_source_blocks.text: He took power in 1996 after staging a bloodless coup against his father, and went on to transform Qatar into the gas-rich power it is today.

Sheikh Hamad during a two-day visit to Bulgaria as part of a European tour in 2009 Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former leader of Qatar, has died aged 74, the country's government announced on Sunday. "The Bureau of the Emir mourns the great loss to the nation of the late, may God have mercy on him," a statement read. Sheikh Hamad was one of the key masterminds behind modern Qatar and had taken power from his father in June 1995 in a bloodless coup. He is credited with transforming its economy into the wealthy global powerhouse it is today, thanks to its huge natural gas reserves. Sheikh Hamad voluntarily abdicated for his son in 2013. Funeral prayers will be held on Sunday evening before several days of public mourning across the country to mark his death.

Former Emir of Qatar Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani dies aged 74 From a tiny state struggling to survive to a country punching above its weight with soft power, wealth and influence felt in the region and beyond, Qatar and its success story were propelled by late Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani. Sheikh Hamad, who died on Sunday aged 74, was able to redefine Qatar’s position on the political map of the Middle East, moving it from the margins of the Gulf to regional prominence in the political, diplomatic, national and humanitarian fields, relying on his vision that transcended the country’s modest size and narrow borders.

The former leader of Qatar, Father Amir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, passed away on Sunday, July 12. In a statement, the Amiri Diwan announced the visionary Emir passed away on the morning of July 12, corresponding to 27 Muharram 1448 AH, at the age of 74. Funeral prayers for Sheikh Hamad are set to take place after Maghrib prayer on Sunday, July 12, at the Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahab Mosque, after which his body will be laid to rest in the Lusail Cemetery. Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels. The Gulf state announced a four-day mourning period, with flags set to be flown at half-mast during this time.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Sheikh Hamad during a two-day visit to Bulgaria as part of a European tour in 2009

Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former leader of Qatar, has died aged 74, the country's government announced on Sunday.

"The Bureau of the Emir mourns the great loss to the nation of the late, may God have mercy on him," a statement read.

Sheikh Hamad was one of the key masterminds behind modern Qatar and had taken power from his father in June 1995 in a bloodless coup.

He is credited with transforming its economy into the wealthy global powerhouse it is today, thanks to its huge natural gas reserves. Sheikh Hamad voluntarily abdicated for his son in 2013.

Funeral prayers will be held on Sunday evening before several days of public mourning across the country to mark his death.

Flags will be flown at half mast, while government officers and public institutions will be shut as a mark of respect.

When Sheikh Hamad took power 31 years ago Qatar was struggling for money with its oil reserves dwindling.

His coup - carried out while his father Sheikh Khalifa was abroad - changed the country forever.

It became a leading producer and exporter of liquefied natural gas, thanks to international partnerships and investments that had been brokered.

In 1996 Al Jazeera was launched there before becoming a big name in international broadcasting.

And Sheikh Hamad founded the Qatar Investment Authority which put money into businesses abroad, including Harrods and football team Paris Saint-Germain.

Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al Thani and his wife Sheikha Moza Bint Nasser al-Misnad hold a copy of the World Cup trophy after Qatar won the right to host the 2022 tournament back in 2010

It would be football where he secured one of Qatar's biggest - and controversial - triumphs.

The country was awarded the right to host the 2022 World Cup in 2010, despite allegations of corruption it was later cleared of.

It hired 30,000 foreign labourers just to build the stadiums. In 2021 it was reported some 6,500 migrant workers from India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka had died since it won the World Cup bid.

The Qatar government said not all the deaths recorded were of people working on World Cup-related projects and many had lived there a long time.

There was also criticism over Qatar's human rights record and laws against same-sex relationships.

Qatar was a British protectorate until 1971, with the Al Thani family as monarchs since 1851.

Within a few years, he laid the foundations for Qatar's rapid development. Although the country is only about one-third the size of Belgium, it possesses one of the world's largest natural gas reserves.

payload.title: Qatarin entinen emiiri Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani on kuollut 74-vuotiaana
payload.summary: Qatarin entinen emiiri Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani kuoli sunnuntaina 74-vuotiaana. Häntä pidetään keskeisenä vaikuttajana Qatarin taloudellisen vaurauden ja kansainvälisen aseman vahvistumisessa.
payload.content:
Qatarin entinen emiiri šeikki Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani on kuollut 74-vuotiaana. Qatarin hallitsijan kanslia ilmoitti hänen kuolleen sunnuntaiaamuna 12. heinäkuuta. Vuosina 1995–2013 maata johtanut Hamad vaikutti ratkaisevasti siihen, että pienestä Persianlahden valtiosta tuli maakaasuvaroihinsa tukeutuva vauras ja alueellisesti vaikutusvaltainen maa.

## Valta vaihtui verettömässä vallankaappauksessa

Hamad nousi Qatarin johtoon kesäkuussa 1995 syrjäytettyään isänsä verettömässä vallankaappauksessa. Hän pysyi emiirinä vuoteen 2013 saakka, jolloin hän luopui vallasta vapaaehtoisesti poikansa hyväksi. Valtakauden päätyttyä Hamadista käytettiin isäemiirin arvonimeä.

Häntä pidetään yhtenä nykyisen Qatarin keskeisistä rakentajista. Hamadin valtakaudella maa hyödynsi mittavia maakaasuvarantojaan ja muutti niiden tuottamat tulot huomattavaksi taloudelliseksi vauraudeksi. Qatar kehittyi maailmanlaajuisesti merkittäväksi taloudelliseksi toimijaksi, vaikka valtio on kooltaan pieni.

## Qatarin vaikutusvalta kasvoi Lähi-idässä

Taloudellisen muutoksen rinnalla Qatar vahvisti asemaansa Lähi-idän poliittisella kartalla. Maa siirtyi Persianlahden marginaalista näkyväksi alueelliseksi toimijaksi, jonka poliittinen, diplomaattinen ja humanitaarinen vaikutus ulottui myös sen rajojen ulkopuolelle. Hamadin johtajuuden on katsottu nostaneen Qatarin kansainvälistä painoarvoa huomattavasti maan vaatimattomaan kokoon nähden.

Al Jazeeran kuvauksen mukaan Hamadin kaudella Qatar muuttui selviytymisestään kamppailleesta pienestä valtiosta maaksi, jonka vauraus, pehmeä valta ja vaikutus tuntuvat sekä Lähi-idässä että sen ulkopuolella. Hänen linjansa vahvisti Qatarin näkyvyyttä poliittisissa ja diplomaattisissa kysymyksissä sekä kansallisessa ja humanitaarisessa toiminnassa.

## Hautajaiset ja neljän päivän suruaika

Hautajaisrukous järjestetään sunnuntai-iltana Maghrib-rukouksen jälkeen Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahab -moskeijassa. Sen jälkeen Hamad haudataan Lusailin hautausmaalle. Qatar on julistanut hänen kuolemansa vuoksi neljän päivän suruajan, jonka aikana maan liput pidetään puolitangossa.

Hallitsijan kanslia kutsui Hamadin kuolemaa suureksi menetykseksi Qatarille. Sunnuntaiaamuna 12. heinäkuuta tapahtunut kuolema ajoittui islamilaisessa kalenterissa päivään 27. muharramkuuta vuonna 1448. Hamadin perintö näkyy erityisesti Qatarin energiavaroihin perustuvassa taloudellisessa muutoksessa sekä maan poliittisen, diplomaattisen ja humanitaarisen vaikutusvallan kasvussa.

Hän johti Qataria vuosina 1995–2013 ja vahvisti maan taloudellista sekä kansainvälistä asemaa.
Qatar julisti neljän päivän suruajan, ja Hamad haudataan Lusailin hautausmaalle.
payload.journalist_note: Lähteet ovat yhteneväisiä kuolemasta, iästä, valtakauden päättymisestä, hautajaisjärjestelyistä ja suruajasta. Paketin lyhyessä kuvauksessa valtaannousun vuodeksi mainitaan 1996, mutta yksityiskohtainen lähdeaineisto ajoittaa verettömän vallankaappauksen kesäkuuhun 1995; artikkelissa käytetään täsmällisemmin tuettua vuotta 1995.

He took power in 1996 after staging a bloodless coup against his father, and went on to transform Qatar into the gas-rich power it is today.

Sheikh Hamad during a two-day visit to Bulgaria as part of a European tour in 2009 Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the former leader of Qatar, has died aged 74, the country's government announced on Sunday. "The Bureau of the Emir mourns the great loss to the nation of the late, may God have mercy on him," a statement read. Sheikh Hamad was one of the key masterminds behind modern Qatar and had taken power from his father in June 1995 in a bloodless coup. He is credited with transforming its economy into the wealthy global powerhouse it is today, thanks to its huge natural gas reserves. Sheikh Hamad voluntarily abdicated for his son in 2013. Funeral prayers will be held on Sunday evening before several days of public mourning across the country to mark his death.

Former Emir of Qatar Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani dies aged 74 From a tiny state struggling to survive to a country punching above its weight with soft power, wealth and influence felt in the region and beyond, Qatar and its success story were propelled by late Father Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani. Sheikh Hamad, who died on Sunday aged 74, was able to redefine Qatar’s position on the political map of the Middle East, moving it from the margins of the Gulf to regional prominence in the political, diplomatic, national and humanitarian fields, relying on his vision that transcended the country’s modest size and narrow borders.

The former leader of Qatar, Father Amir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, passed away on Sunday, July 12. In a statement, the Amiri Diwan announced the visionary Emir passed away on the morning of July 12, corresponding to 27 Muharram 1448 AH, at the age of 74. Funeral prayers for Sheikh Hamad are set to take place after Maghrib prayer on Sunday, July 12, at the Imam Muhammad bin Abdul Wahab Mosque, after which his body will be laid to rest in the Lusail Cemetery.
